newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soy products sharply lower on Brazil imports.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soy products sharply lower on Brazil imports.

text.p: CBOT soymeal and soyoil futures were sharply lower at midsession on Wednesday in response to confirmation that at least one major U.S. firm was importing soybeans from Brazil, traders said.
Citing extremely tight U.S. soybean supplies, Cargill, Inc issued a statement that said the company had contracted to import soybeans from Brazil.
Cargill declined to provide details of the transaction.
The news triggered sharp losses across the soy complex.
Brazilian processor Ceval also confirmed on Wednesday that it was in talks to sell 40,000 tonnes of soymeal to an unnamed source in the U.S.

The import of Brazil soybeans and soymeal has prompted ideas that demand for U.S. products will fall off, even though "the amounts that are coming in aren't enough to change the balance sheet," said a floor trader.
In early trading, Refco sold 300 lots July soymeal, 200 lots August and 200 September and R.J. O'Brien sold 300 July and 200 August, pit sources said.
At 1135 CDT, soymeal futures were $8.20 to $1.30 lower with July down $8.20 at $274.70 per ton. Soyoil futures were down 0.20 to 0.46 cent per lb, with July down 0.46 at 23.39.
